Music 0.11 (build 12) adds interactive clear CD cases to the offline music player.

## What's new

- Albums keep the two-column layout and display artwork printed on discs inside reflective clear cases.
- Hold an album to open the CD browser. Drag to tilt, open or close the lid, flip through albums, and use the landscape layout for a larger view.
- Now Playing displays the current song's artwork on a spinning CD. Spin follows playback, device motion gently tilts the case, and tapping the case opens or closes it.
- The renderer and its dependencies are bundled in the app and work offline. Native Liquid Glass navigation and controls, Cask scrolling settings, lyrics, themes, and library data are retained.

Download Music.ipa and use your existing LiveContainer or signing/sideloading setup. Replace the existing Music installation and keep the same data container to retain songs, playlists, and settings. The bundle identifier remains com.billy.glassmusic. Minimum iOS version: 16.0; native Liquid Glass requires supported newer iOS versions.

This is the same verified IPA delivered for Music 0.11 (12), with an ad-hoc signature for your installer to handle.

Native compilation, linking, Objective-C startup layout, archive contents, and 227 signature code pages passed verification. Eighteen actual browser WebGL renderer checks passed, including offline loading, spinning/pausing, lid opening, artwork replacement, reduced motion, and failure handling. The attached reports record the results.

Physical iPhone testing is still required for WebKit/GPU performance, device-motion calibration, gestures, landscape behavior, and energy use. Browser renderer checks do not substitute for an iPhone run.

versions.localizedDescription:
Generate and edit images with AI. Prism 1.2 adds LoRAs for FLUX.2 Klein 4B and Z-Image Turbo, with an orange native Liquid Glass library and Civitai browser.

## What's new

- Tap **Add LoRA** on Generate or Edit. The library's top-right **+** opens a native browser with preview images, search, sorting, and a download button on each row.
- Results follow the selected model: **Flux.2 Klein 4B** or **ZImageTurbo**. A filtered Civitai website view is also available from the menu.
- Download adapters directly, or import compatible `.safetensors` files from Files. Installed adapters and thumbnails remain available offline.
- Enable up to three adapters per model and adjust each strength from 0–200%. FLUX adapters also work with reference-image editing. Saved artwork records the adapters and strengths used.
- Optional **Connect Civitai** verifies a personal API key and stores it in this device's Keychain. The account sheet links to Civitai's official account page. Mature listings require a connected account and remain subject to Civitai's account settings and access restrictions.

Adapters use streamed low-rank projections alongside the existing 4-bit models. Downloads verify the selected file's SHA-256 and validate its tensor layout before installation. Standard supported LoRA exports are accepted; incompatible architectures and unsupported adapter variants produce an explanation instead of being applied to the wrong model. Individual adapter files are limited to 1 GiB.

This update retains the orange icon, the previous High-quality and decoder-memory changes, downloaded base models, and saved artwork. Update the existing Prism app/data container to retain your downloads and gallery.

## iPhone download

Download the attached **Prism.ipa**. It is the actual unsigned arm64 iPhone app, version **1.2 (3)**, for **iOS 26 or later**. Use your existing LiveContainer or signing/sideloading setup. Model weights are downloaded separately inside Prism.

## Verification

[The native build](https://github.com/Strezzy/Prism/actions/runs/38204695329) passed **67 XCTest checks with zero failures**, with one explicit unsupported-GPU skip. Checks include the production Keychain credential lifecycle, model-specific LoRA layouts, file validation, persistence, and Civitai filtering. **114 CPU reference cases** passed. All six native screenshots were reviewed, including working live preview images and the clean account screen. The downloaded iPhone IPA independently passed metadata, executable, dependency, resource, and checksum inspection.

Version 1.9.5 adds a centered voice orb with reactive particles and reversible chat scattering, while suspending chat rendering during voice mode. Version 1.9.6 fixes chat visibility by limiting the voice scatter shader to individual message surfaces during transitions. Version 1.9.7 reduces voice response waits and adds a darker maroon voice scene, inward listening motion, denser rear particles and occasional neural connections.

# Loop 1.3.1 (build 8): rebuilt portrait and atmosphere effects

## Finishing fixes

Edge expansion and contraction now operate locally on the matte boundary, without raising empty background or making an opaque subject translucent. Weather uses a spatial particle neighborhood instead of evaluating the entire particle set for every output pixel. Face edits are composed before body deformation, so the transformed face follows the body. Foreground stabilization responds immediately to a changed stability setting. These refinements retain the new model-based effects described below.

## Replaced, not repainted

The illustrated face masks and flat body silhouettes from 1.2 are removed. The existing cinematic grades, lens looks, crop and overlay tools, video exports and full-video import default remain.

Face presets now deform the source image: face width, jaw, chin, eyes, nose and lips, plus edge-preserving skin smoothing, detail and tone. Each has adjustable controls. Mature and Older use a bundled, converted Fast-AgingGAN Core ML model. Youthful Retouch is explicitly a retouch preset, not trained age regression. Automatic face blur and pixelation are available; review detections before relying on privacy protection.

Body presets use pose-guided source-pixel reshaping for waist, shoulders, hips, torso, arms and legs. They do not paint a body-shaped texture over the subject, invent clothing, or reconstruct hidden limbs. Strong shape edits can distort nearby scenery.

## Cleaner foreground separation

Studio quality uses bundled MODNet portrait alpha matting, source-guided edge refinement and motion-gated temporal stabilization. Accurate native matting remains available. Foreground-object mode can protect salient non-person objects. Edge, feather and stability controls plus preview-only mask inspection help with difficult clips. Seeking and changing direction reset temporal state rather than reusing an unrelated silhouette.

## Layered atmosphere and photographic backgrounds

All ten atmosphere effects use the new GPU renderer, including soft rain streaks, depth-scaled snow, embers, fireflies, confetti, refractive bubbles, volumetric-style fog and light leaks. Choose layered, behind-subject or foreground placement and adjust density, size, speed and wind. Rear particles are occluded by the foreground mask. This is layered compositing, not full 3D scene reconstruction.

Six CC0 photographic backgrounds from Poly Haven join the retained background collection. Photographic backgrounds support framing and zoom; background blur, exposure and warmth can be adjusted. The six embedded photographs are 2560 x 1440 perspective projections of original 4K HDRI assets. Imported photos retain the existing up-to-4096-pixel support.

## Offline, exports and compatibility

All shaders, models and photographic assets are bundled. No account, runtime downloads or server rendering. Existing GIF/APNG/MP4/HEVC output, audio rules, trimming, crop tracking and overlay timing remain. New video imports still select the complete clip. Old projects continue to open; retired illustrated-effect identifiers are ignored, while other edits are preserved.

Neural aging processes a 512-pixel face crop, then composites it into the source-resolution frame. It does not generate native-4K facial detail or guarantee an exact age, identity preservation, flicker-free motion or real-time playback. Heavy effects can reduce preview rate and slow export. HDR sources still export as SDR.

## Verification

The release requires native arm64 compilation and package verification, plus a separate focused XCTest run covering shaders, source-pixel warps, foreground occlusion, deterministic animation, bundled models, migration and photographic assets. A real portrait fixture also exercises detection, matting and rendering. Reports record actual results. The long full-editor UI suite and physical-iPhone validation are not claimed. Model conversion parity checks ran with native Core ML

Create GIFs and full-color APNG animations locally on iPhone and iPad. Native SwiftUI and Liquid Glass, with a teal-and-lime identity alongside the other Strezzy apps.

Import from Photos or Files, trim, adjust portrait/landscape/square crops, choose resolution and frame rate, and export. Includes reverse and ping-pong playback, speed, loop count, adaptive GIF palettes and dithering, local projects and an export library.

Add circular or rectangular blur, pixelation, solid covers, emoji and text. Overlays can be timed, tracked on device with Vision and adjusted with manual keyframes. Review tracked content before sharing; tracking is not infallible.

**Format limits:** GIF delays use 10 ms steps. The 60 FPS option samples 60 frames per second and approximates their timing; some viewers play fast GIFs more slowly. APNG offers finer timing and full color, subject to the receiving app's support. Both formats are silent. Native/custom resolution is capped at a 4096-pixel longest edge, with a 30,000-frame export guard. Supported input depends on the iPhone's video decoders. Cloud-only source items must first be downloaded through their provider.

**Install:** `Loop.ipa` is an arm64 iPhone package for the existing sideloading/signing workflow. Requires iOS 26 or later. No account, subscription, ads, watermark, analytics, model downloads or app-initiated network requests.

**Validation:** Native arm64 compilation and automated simulator tests are attached as reports. Physical iPhone thermals, long high-resolution exports and SideStore/LiveContainer behavior have not been tested on a physical device in this build session.

The complete source archive and generated Xcode project are attached. Existing apps and historical releases are preserved.

# Orbit 1.0

A full-screen spatial-video viewer with two-axis tilt depth, portrait and landscape playback, Photos/Files import, a local library, touch look-around, depth strength, recenter, fit/fill, scrubbing, mute and looping. Native ice-blue/violet Liquid Glass interface; processing stays on device. Requires iOS 26.

The arm64 IPA is unsigned for the existing sideloading workflow. Use original spatial recordings; ordinary or flattened videos play in 2D. Depth is a bounded custom stereo reconstruction, with possible artifacts around occlusions, reflections and low-texture areas.

## Validation

The native Release IPA was successfully built at `564d52ddfc4e433f73737347624cf18c5d1abefb`. The original functional tests at `8abeda5be908b06b3a49c715d06d6d142f6d34fe` recorded **7 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped**. The app, playback, renderer, unit-test, project and icon sources are identical between these commits. Those existing results are reused; no new test execution is claimed. The skipped check is real stereo MV-HEVC decoding, unsupported by the simulator. The GPU disparity test and portrait/landscape rotation and import-control assertions passed.

Only the verified original portrait capture is attached. The incorrectly cropped landscape capture is omitted. A later screenshot retry timed out during simulator/test-runner preparation before assertions were recorded; it is not counted as a pass. Physical iPhone depth quality, motion, thermals and sideload-host behavior remain untested.

The source archive matches the packaged native build and includes the XcodeGen project specification.
